title: Albumin-binding dendrimer-conjugated siRNA enables safe and effective gene silencing throughout the central nervous system.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplementary package (9.3 MB). It contains only 10 figure images (.gif/.webp) and one 8.6 MB PDF. I extracted the PDF text with pdfminer: 13 pages, 6,021 characters, 38 embedded images and zero extractable table cells - every panel, including Supplementary Table S1 (the siRNA sequences), is a rasterised image. No CSV, TSV, XLSX or any other tabular file exists anywhere in the package. I also checked the paper's data availability statement, every accession mentioned in the full text, Europe PMC's text-mined accessions, NCBI links to GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample/dbGaP, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI: all returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Group sizes (n = 2-6 animals per group, read from figure legends in the full text and the supplementary PDF), the identity of the four target genes (HTT, APP, JAK1, MECP2), the three siRNA scaffolds compared (unconjugated, divalent, dendrimer), and the assay types (QuantiGene 2.0 for mRNA, peptide nucleic acid hybridisation assay for tissue siRNA accumulation). I could not verify any of these against a data file because no data file exists.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, and this kills it. The data availability statement reads verbatim: 'All data are presented in the main text and the supplementary data, with raw data available from the corresponding authors upon request.' I opened the entire supplement and it is images only - a 13-page PDF of figure panels plus 10 figure graphics. There is no repository deposit: no GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus), SRA (Sequence Read Archive), BioProject, Zenodo or Dryad record is linked from the paper or found by searching the DOI. 'Available on request' is an explicit A1 fail condition in the checklist.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The candidate label - percentage of messenger RNA (mRNA) remaining after gene silencing, and tissue siRNA concentration - exists only as bar heights and scatter points inside raster figure images. It is not a column anywhere; it would have to be constructed by digitising pixels off plots, which is inference across sources in the worst sense.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. The siRNA sequences and chemical modification patterns (the only plausible model input) are in Supplementary Table S1, which is an embedded image with no extractable text. They would have to be transcribed by hand or by optical character recognition, and a single misread modification code (m, f, #, C12, C6, SB, V) silently corrupts the input.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the figure legends - mRNA as percent remaining relative to a non-targeting control, siRNA accumulation in nanograms per gram of tissue, dose in nanomoles and micrograms. This is the one Part A item that passes, but it passes on the paper text, not on a file.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL by a wide margin. Group sizes are n = 2-6 animals throughout (n = 3 mice/group, n = 4-6 mice/group, n = 5-6 rats/group, n = 2-3 rats/group). With 3 siRNA scaffolds, 4 target genes and roughly 10-15 anatomical regions, the absolute ceiling is a few hundred animal-region measurements, and the independent unit is the animal - likely under 150. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for pure classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits - the entire supplement is 9.3 MB. This is irrelevant given there is nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed, which the checklist treats as a fail. There is no download whose counts could be compared against the paper's claims; the only numbers available are the ones the paper states about itself.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: the silencing label comes from a physical measurement (QuantiGene 2.0 branched-DNA mRNA assay) and tissue accumulation from a peptide nucleic acid hybridisation assay. Neither is another model's output nor computable from the features. A8 is the one real strength here, and it is wasted because the measurements were never deposited.

existing_models.name: FRAMEs (fast activity prediction of chemically modified siRNAs, Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to combine deep-learning structure prediction with physics-based energy terms and inference-augmented tabular deep learning; its energy score correlates with measured IC50 (half-maximal inhibitory concentration) and melting temperature. I read the abstract listing only, not the paper, so I did not verify a specific number or split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Data scarcity for fully chemically modified siRNA, which is why they resort to inference augmentation.

existing_models.name: Cm-siRPred and ENsiRNA (chemically modified siRNA efficacy predictors; ENsiRNA is a geometric graph neural network, Journal of Molecular Biology 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified - found as search hits only, I did not retrieve the papers or check their reported numbers.

existing_models.name: Review: 'From rules to foundation models' (NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2026), covering 40+ siRNA design models
existing_models.score_and_split: A survey, not a model. It states that delivery context - lipid nanoparticle formulation, GalNAc (N-acetylgalactosamine) conjugation, tissue targeting - drives potency in ways sequence-level models do not capture, and that leakage-aware splitting is needed because benchmarks are inflated.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Predicting the behaviour of fully modified, therapeutically relevant siRNA, and capturing delivery/tissue context rather than sequence alone.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a nucleotide language model could in principle encode siRNA sequences, but chemical modifications (2'-O-methyl, 2'-fluoro, phosphorothioate, dendrimer conjugate) are outside every public backbone's alphabet
backbone.hardware: Not applicable - with fewer than ~150 independent animals there is nothing to fit a head on.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. A siRNA efficacy table such as the Huesken dataset or the modified-siRNA sets behind Cm-siRPred would be the natural partner, but those measure unmodified or differently modified siRNA knockdown in cell culture, not dendrimer-conjugate biodistribution in rodent brain.
integration.join_key: None available - the siRNA sequences are locked inside a figure image, so there is no identifier to join on without manual transcription.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with three scaffolds and four targets measured in a handful of animals, no join produces a question that generalises beyond this one paper's experiment.

controls.positive_control: The paper itself contains good biological controls (non-targeting control siRNA, artificial cerebrospinal fluid vehicle, the known divalent-siRNA scaffold as a benchmark), but a control is only useful to an ML project if the underlying numbers are obtainable, and they are not.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size - with n = 3 per group, a shuffled-label model and a real one are statistically indistinguishable.
controls.external_validation: None. The siRNA scaffolds and the dendrimer conjugate chemistry are specific to this laboratory (the Khvorova/Watts group at UMass Chan), and no independent dataset measures the same quantity the same way.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available, because no model can be trained: the only claim the data could support is 'in 3-6 mice per group from one laboratory, dendrimer-conjugated siRNA silenced four target genes about as well as the divalent scaffold', and that is the paper's own finding, stated by statistics rather than by prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use siRNA sequence and chemical attachment type to predict how much a gene is silenced in each brain region.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model, for each experiment, the small interfering RNA sequence, its chemical modification pattern, which carrier molecule is attached (none, divalent, or dendrimer), the dose, the injection route and the brain region sampled. The number of examples is at most a few hundred animal-region measurements and realistically under 150 independent animals - and none of them are in a readable file.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be percent target messenger RNA (mRNA) remaining relative to a non-targeting control, measured by the QuantiGene 2.0 branched-DNA assay, alongside siRNA tissue concentration measured by a peptide nucleic acid hybridisation assay. Both are genuine lab measurements, but both exist only as bar heights in figure images.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, groups developing central nervous system RNA therapeutics could rank carrier chemistries before running rodent studies, saving months of animal work; even a failed model would quantify how much brain-region-to-region variability is predictable. Neither is achievable from this paper, which has no deposited data.

more_or_better_data.why: The existing siRNA activity models (FRAMEs, Cm-siRPred, ENsiRNA) are trained on hundreds to thousands of measured knockdown values. This paper offers at most a few hundred animal-region readings across 3 scaffolds and 4 genes, and offers none of them in machine-readable form.

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist (n = 2-6 animals per group) and could in principle estimate measurement noise, but with 3 animals per group the noise estimate is itself too noisy to calibrate anything, and the replicate values are not released - only means and standard deviations drawn as error bars.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant here, since we cannot field a competitor. The field's own 2026 review explicitly flags that delivery and tissue context are unmodelled, which would have been the opening - but exploiting it needs a biodistribution dataset with hundreds of distinct chemistries, not three.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Every condition fails: we cannot run an existing model as a baseline on these data, our model would not see a superset of its inputs, this paper's in vivo rodent brain assay measures a different quantity from the cell-culture knockdown assays those models were trained on, and there is no shared evaluation split or join key.

ml_idea: The intended idea was to predict regional gene silencing in the central nervous system from siRNA chemistry, carrier scaffold, dose, route and anatomical region. It is dead on arrival for this paper: the measurements were never deposited. The idea is worth remembering for a different source - a dataset that pooled dozens of oligonucleotide conjugate chemistries with regional biodistribution and silencing across many animals would address exactly the gap the 2026 NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics review names, namely that sequence-level siRNA models ignore delivery context.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset. The only measured quantity is the supplement size: 9.3 MB of images, with 6,021 characters of extractable PDF text and zero table cells.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement, then unzip the supplement and list the file extensions. Both took under two minutes and both kill it: 'raw data available from the corresponding authors upon request', and the package contains only .gif, .webp and one image-only .pdf.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A1 outright: no data is deposited anywhere and the paper routes raw data through 'available from the corresponding authors upon request', which the checklist names as an explicit fail. I verified this by unzipping the full supplement - it is 10 figure images plus a 13-page PDF whose 38 embedded graphics include Supplementary Table S1, so even the siRNA sequences are pixels rather than text. It also fails A2 (the silencing label exists only as bar heights to be digitised), A3 (inputs are an image of a table) and A5 by a wide margin (n = 2-6 animals per group; at most a few hundred animal-region readings against a ~1,500-row floor). This is a well-executed in vivo pharmacology paper whose scientific contribution is real, but it is a small-n animal study, not a dataset.
